A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EditVerse and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding methods, experiments, and supporting material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, human preferences in Figure 5, training-data and architecture ablations, and additional image/video experiments in Appendix A.3.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and additionally reports human–VLM correlation and inference-resource measurements in Appendices A.2 and A.5.

M1.justification: The architecture, interleaved inputs, four-dimensional RoPE, and training/inference procedures remain unchanged. RoPE dimensions are reordered only in the explanation. The corrected loss equation matches the MSE objective already stated in v1; compression, token selection, and distillation remain future proposals.

E1.justification: Training tasks and the six evaluation benchmarks remain unchanged. Table 10 revises dataset descriptions and provenance; v1 Section 4 already cites the customization source. The token-length efficiency sweep does not establish a new task or data population.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 2, 3, and 6–9, including LucyEdit and Runway Aleph on EditVerseBench. Newly cited concurrent works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix A.5 adds resource profiling at 17,652, 34,342, 63,662, and 110,822 tokens with 20-step and 50-step inference. Existing benchmark protocols and Section 5.1 training settings remain unchanged. Added participant information documents the existing user study rather than establishing a changed sample size.

E4.justification: v3 adds an analysis of memory and latency scaling with token length and a quantitative comparison between human preferences and VLM evaluation. Existing training-data ablations, architecture ablations, emergent-ability examples, and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix A.2 introduces Pearson correlation as a statistical agreement summary and newly discloses three independent judgments per comparison. It explicitly acknowledges that formal inter-annotator agreement was not computed. No confidence intervals or increase in collected judgments is established.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores, ablation results, and Figure 5 preferences are unchanged. New results include Pearson correlation 0.84 and Table 11 resource measurements: across the token-length sweep, memory rises from 29,511 to 44,824 MB and 50-step latency from 52 to 873 seconds. These are additional measurements, not improved same-setting performance.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 corrects the displayed flow-matching loss from an unsquared norm to squared error, resolving its mismatch with the existing MSE description. This is a limited mathematical correction; no new theorem, formal assumption, or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning unified image/video generation and editing, cross-modal transfer, emergent abilities, the data pipeline, EditVerseBench, and leading editing performance.

C2.justification: Appendix A.5 expands the computational-cost discussion with an interpretation of measured scaling as manageable, clarification that performance is unoptimized, and specific efficiency proposals. Appendix A.2 explains the rationale for minimally instructed non-expert judges and acknowledges missing agreement analysis. Existing substantive failure and applicability limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 specifies an external annotation vendor, 20 non-expert annotators, 150 comparisons per annotator, and three judgments per pair. It discloses 8× VAE spatial downsampling and resource measurements. Table 10 aligns customization provenance with OmniVCus and generalizes the rendered-video description; these do not establish changed training data.

R1.justification: v3 adds FullDiT2 to the token-selection discussion and four concurrent video-editing references in the dataset-quality discussion: Wei, Mou, Bai, and Yang (2025). The main related-work section and central novelty positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized edits reorder the RoPE explanation, correct the vision-channel symbol and OursMethod placeholder, expand appendix explanations, and update affiliations and acknowledgements. The overall section sequence and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the two-panel efficiency Figure 10 and Table 11. Appendix material is locally resized and reflowed, including Table 7. Existing Figures 1–9 and benchmark-table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency through clearer user-study reporting, quantified human–VLM agreement, resource measurements, and corrections to the loss equation and dataset provenance. These address bounded reporting gaps in v1. Missing profiling hardware and repetition details, absent statistical uncertainty, and the limited scaling sweep constrain the strength of the added evidence.
